Cell round 4: space age, made modern

Brief 012 round 4 · Forma · 2026-10-15 · Codex only (ceiling total $1.809 of $3.00). Faces, bodies, hair, signature items and silhouette shapes kept; animation rules kept (hems at hip or mid-thigh, no capes or tails, ponytail one chain). Thumbnails embedded; click for full files; model, prompt, refs, sha256 in PROVENANCE.json.

Summary

Round 3b drifted into generic modern tactical (khaki, moss, chestnut, ripstop, canvas). Round 4 goes back to space-age couture pushed forward with modern construction: white and silver base, vinyl, patent, lacquer, bonded and quilted panels, moulded yokes and collars, ring pulls and round buckles, white boots, gauntlets. Each person takes a different corner of that vocabulary and one bold hero colour; the team thread is the white-and-silver base and the porthole lamp. Top lineup: L4, the hero-block set (each person's colour as the main garment). The first three lineups, with the hero colour only as trim, read at 50 px as one white squad; L4 reads as four people (section 5).

Team thread: white (cool, not the city's cream) and brushed silver, charcoal only for small parts, plus the porthole lamp motif (a chrome ring around a lens that glows soft pale aqua; it lights when that person acts), worn on the pack shell, the ring collar, the visor and the belt buckle. At 50 px the lamp is a small emissive dot: as paint it is lost, as a game sprite with bloom it works.

2. Colour

Gate: dE2000 20 or more from cone red #e03a2f, guard amber #f0a020, rival violet #8a4fd0 (unlit). Every bright blue that clears the rivals' violet lands within 15 of the city's cobalt or turquoise enamels, and the greens and pinks sit near the city's park green and flamingo; that is flagged below, not avoidable. The base is cool white, not the city's cream (dE 9.8 from cream).

3. Takes

Four per person: three explorations with the hero colour as trim, and a hero-block take with the colour as the main garment (the one I recommend).

Animation notes (estimates from the drawings; no rig built)

Base rig: 65-bone Mixamo humanoid. Extra bones are over those 65. Vinyl, patent, lacquer and quilting are shader and normal-map work on skinned rigid shells; no garment needs a cloth sim. The lamps are emissive materials (0 bones), driven by the 'acting' state.

4. Lamp motif and lineups

Lamp bead kept and styled as a porthole lamp: a chrome ring around a pale-aqua lens. It reads in all four lineups at close range (Scout pack, Fixer collar, Tech visor, Enforcer belt buckle and rifle).

The comparison row

5. Silhouette test at 50 px

Black fills and the whole lineup at play scale (tallest figure 56 px after the 38 degree foreshortening), native size and 5x. Profile distance: how different the width-over-height outlines are (higher = more distinct; the closest pair matters). IoU: true-scale overlap (lower = more distinct). Figures: 0 Scout, 1 Fixer, 2 Tech, 3 Enforcer.

The cut of the colour block, not the garment shape, is what makes them separable.

7. Iteration log

First hero colours (lime #a8d234, rose #f58fb0) painted too close to guard amber and cone red (22.8 and 20.4); Scout and Fixer redrawn with a greener lime and a cooler pink, then the lineups and the two sheets redone.
